title: The firefighting system of the Van der Heyden brothers in 17th century Amsterdam
summary: This article explores how the Van der Heyden brothers pioneered an innovative firefighting system in 17th century Amsterdam, a city prone to devastating fires due to its wooden architecture and dense urban layout. Their system introduced organized fire brigades, specialized equipment, and coordinated community response that became a model for urban fire safety.
problem_solved: Provided Amsterdam with an organized, systematic approach to firefighting in a densely built wooden city prone to catastrophic fires.
why_valuable: It documents how early modern urban innovation solved critical public safety challenges and influenced firefighting practices for centuries to come.
